subject: EdgeMetrics deployment strategy & migration follow-up
messages:
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@edgemetrics.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: EdgeMetrics deployment questions after today's call

Hi Monica —

Thanks again for the intro/demo today. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions as we scope next steps: 

Summary of our current state:
- We run a self-hosted inference API (wrapper around an open model fork) on an internal GPU cluster (NVIDIA A100s).
- Two clusters: staging (~4 nodes) and prod (~10 nodes). Peak p95 latency ~420ms for 2k token requests.
- We also produce embeddings via the same service; those are stored in S3.
- Compliance: SOC 2 in progress; data residency required in us-east-1 for certain datasets.

Primary goals:
1) Reduce unit cost for high-volume summarization and embedding workloads.
2) Improve latency and scale predictably during weekly spikes.
3) Maintain strict data controls for PII-sensitive workloads.

Questions for Redwood (short list):
- Is the Hosted API an acceptable option for a pilot if we disable token logging and keep data residency in a dedicated region? Or will our PII requirements force Dedicated/Private from day one?
- If Dedicated is the likely production target, what does the migration path look like from our self-hosted API (what breaks, what we can reuse)?
- For Private VPC/on-prem: what's required for on-prem packaging? Are there suggested baseline hardware profiles?
- Any red flags around model compatibility (we use a custom tokenizer layer and minor model changes) and quantization?

Attaching a short infra summary we promised. Can you send a migration checklist and a timeline estimate for a small POC (2 weeks)?

Thanks — happy to set a follow-up call.

Sam
Sam Torres
Head of ML Engineering, EdgeMetrics
sam.torres@edgemetrics.ai
Attachments: edge-current-infra-summary.pdf (1 page)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@edgemetrics.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: EdgeMetrics deployment questions after today's call

Hi Sam —

Great notes — thanks for the infra summary. Below is a pragmatic migration recommendation and the concrete next steps so your team can decide quickly.

Short recommendation (phased):
1) Pilot on Hosted API (2-week POC)
   - Use Redwood Hosted in us-east-1 with token-level logging disabled and request-level metadata only.
   - Purpose: validate integration, measure latency and cost delta vs in-house.
   - This avoids early procurement work and gets your product team measurable numbers fast.

2) Dedicated capacity for production scale
   - If cost/latency are acceptable, move to Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) for predictable throughput and isolation.
   - You keep the same API surface; we provide migration guidance to reuse your model artifacts and tokenizers.

3) Private VPC / on-prem for regulated workloads
   - For datasets that must remain in-customer network, we offer a Private deployment (VPC or on-prem bundle).
   - On-prem: we ship a validated package and playbook; baseline is 8x A100-class GPUs for small production footprints.

Migration considerations (high level):
- Tokenizer compatibility: our runtime supports custom tokenizers; we ask for a small tokenization test corpus to validate token alignment.
- KV cache and state: if your current API relies on long-lived KV caches, we'll map that to Redwood's prefix/KV cache primitives during migration.
- Quantization: we can run a quantization compatibility pass during onboarding; some model variants may require minimal changes.
- Endpoints & routing: we will create versioned model endpoints so you can canary traffic between your old API and Redwood.

Action items I can own this week:
- Send a migration checklist and an onboarding template (attached).
- Schedule a tech deep-dive with Rishi (our inference engineer) to cover tokenizer, model artifacts, and perf goals.
- Provide a preliminary cost/throughput estimate for a 2-week POC.

What we need from you to scope the POC:
- Target qps and peak concurrency (e.g., 50 req/s baseline, 200 req/s spike)
- Typical request distribution and token lengths (median / p95 token counts)
- Which models you want to test (name/version) and whether you can provide model binaries or a test image
- Any PII/data residency constraints per dataset

Attachments: redwood-migration-checklist.xlsx, redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf

If this plan looks good I'll send calendar options for the deep-dive (Rishi + me) and the POC kickoff.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@edgemetrics.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:21:00 -0400
Subject: Re: EdgeMetrics deployment questions after today's call

Sam — quick technical follow-up from my side before the deep-dive: 

1) Model & tokenizer: please share a representative model artifact (or at minimum the tokenizer config) and a 1000-line sample corpus so we can validate tokenization parity and estimated tokenization overhead.

2) Perf signals: do you have a perf trace (latency distribution & CPU/GPU utilization) for a busy hour? That helps us size Dedicated pools and determine batching strategy.

3) Storage/connectors: confirm where embeddings will live post-migration (S3, customer-managed buckets). We support S3 and a few object stores; KMS integration for encryption-at-rest is available.

4) Compatibility: if you rely on custom CUDA kernels or very model-specific ops, note them now — we can run a compatibility pass but extreme custom kernels can slow onboarding.

If you can drop the corpus and perf trace to a shared Drive link (or send to me directly), I'll pre-run a quick compatibility check and bring notes to the deep-dive.

Proposed deep-dive agenda (30–45m):
- Tokenizer parity check + model artifact review (10m)
- Traffic profile and perf targets (10m)
- Migration mechanics: canary routing, KV cache mapping, and rollback strategy (10m)
- Timeline & procurement ask (5–15m)

I can take the first two bullets and produce a short tech-readout within 48 hours of receiving the artifacts.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Team — thanks for the quick turnaround and clear plan. Confirming next steps from EdgeMetrics: 

- We agree to a Hosted API pilot in us-east-1 with token logging disabled for POC. Goal: 2-week POC starting the week of Aug 2.
- Procurement wants a preliminary quote and the Dedicated SLA doc for their packet (cc'd procurement).
- I'll send: sample corpus (1000 lines), a busy-hour perf trace, and a pointer to the S3 bucket we plan to use. Expect those by Fri, Jul 2.
- If the POC meets perf and cost targets, we'll move to Dedicated capacity for production and evaluate a Private VPC for regulated datasets.

Procurement requested a one-page summary of options (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and an estimated timeline for each step — can you send that along with the quote/DocuSign link?

We'll plan to have the technical deep-dive the week of Jul 5. Please share 2–3 calendar slots.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

Sam
